safety.maintainedUnsafeDetail: setting a launcher argument needs no unsafe code

operability.diagnostics: the launcher writes the full launch command to its own instance log, so a wrong argument is visible without Ravel reporting anything
operability.debugWorkflow: an operator edits two instance settings and can remove them again, which makes Ravel switchable off without uninstalling it
operability.crashAttribution: the game process is the launcher's own, so a crash report belongs to the instance the launcher already tracks

prismIntegration.detail: the pinned launcher exposes OverrideJavaArgs and JvmArgs, so the two arguments ADG-1 needs can be set on an instance without changing the launcher. It also exposes OverrideCommands and WrapperCommand, so the rejected hosted-VM candidate would not have needed a patch either. An operator's instance log was read and three substring tests passed on it: `-javaagent:` appears, `-Djava.library.path=` appears, and none of five known mod loader names does. Those three tests are the whole proof. Nothing here checks that the launch was of the pinned 26.1.2, that the launcher was the pinned Prism, that either argument sat on the game's command line rather than elsewhere in the log, or that the client reached a world or exited cleanly.

deviations.summary: an operator's instance log shows the pinned game launching with both of Ravel's arguments and no other mod loader; only the hash of its redacted form is recorded, because a launcher log can carry the account's session arguments
the launcher's settings are read as names in its own 16286664 bytes of executable, which proves the settings exist and not that a given value is accepted
